open_items: SI Tables 1-6 are cited but absent from the supplied PDF, which has no embedded attachments; the c161 entry in supplement-manifest.json lists no files. No separate supplement was located beside the PDF. During reconciliation, urllib requests to the named DOI, Oxford repository record, and OSF registration API all failed with a local socket-permission error (WinError 10013). No supplement or registration was inspected.

SI Table 3 is needed to verify full-sample frequency, flexibility, inaccuracy, and unclarity coefficients, SEs, p-values, model specification, and analysis counts. The main PDF prints only subgroup coefficients for these individual outcomes and no full-sample numerical arm means or SDs (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3.1-3.2).

Total randomized count, AI and Control arm sizes, and outcome-specific contributing participant counts are not printed. The stated final sample of 225 is retained at study level only; estimate-level counts are null (PDF p. 4, Section 2.1).

Participant accounting is internally inconsistent: the paper states 266 completions, forty-three exclusions, and a final sample of 225. The total has not been repaired by arithmetic. The perception-test degrees of freedom on PDF p. 8 are not printed participant counts and were not used to infer any count.
The position of the attention check and whether assignment was stratified by English proficiency and prior ChatGPT experience are not stated (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 2.1-2.2).

For the group-level counts, the treatment of duplicate ideas, domain aggregation, normalization by arm size, contributing participant counts, and uncertainty are not described. SI Table 5 may clarify them (PDF p. 7, Section 3.2.3).

The full-sample labels in the PDF p. 7 prose conflict with Fig. 5: the prose calls 635 versus 552 flexibility and 442 versus 313 frequency. The retained outcome assignments follow the independently checked figure panel labels and legend on PDF p. 9. The figure caption also reverses the use/nonuse wording. Both publication inconsistencies remain documented.

The participant-facing ChatGPT model, tier, access route, and detailed usage instructions are unspecified. The recorded year is the product release year printed in the introduction, not an inferred model year (PDF pp. 1 and 5).
The paper names GPT4o and GPT4 Turbo for automatic scoring without identifying which model supplied the analyzed counts (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3).

The article states that the study was preregistered, but it does not identify a specific preregistered primary outcome; the linked registration could not be inspected (PDF p. 4, Section 2.1; PDF pp. 12-13, Pre-registration).
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10 against the complete 14-page journal PDF and all 656 lines of its markdown conversion, including Appendix A and references. PDF page indexes plus one match printed page numbers. Every cited PDF page was text-extracted with pymupdf; Fig. 5 was additionally rendered and inspected in memory. Source quotes normalize whitespace and discretionary PDF hyphenation. The comparison file reports six matched estimates with no coded-field differences and no estimates unique to either extractor. Resolutions also document independent checks of agreed fields and the two corrections from category_count to automated_score for the individual LLM-scored creativity outcomes. A’s frequency slug is retained for the estimate B names fluency. All six screening outcomes S1-O1 through S1-O6 and their full-sample AI-versus-Control contrasts are represented; no additional eligible outcome or contrast was found. Four individual-output records retain null statistics because full-sample numerical results cannot be verified. The two diversity records retain printed whole-set arm levels; these are not participant means. No effect sizes, differences, sample counts, or figure-coordinate estimates were calculated. Inaccuracy and unclarity are auxiliary output-scored outcomes of the divergent-use task, coded other and excluded from pooling. The pre/post surveys measure perceptions, not later unassisted output; within_person is null for every extracted contrast. Pre-existing English-proficiency/experience groups and post-task HAI usage classes are not additional randomized arms. No shared sample is identified in the screening form. Empty source.fields arrays provide qualitative provenance. The failed urllib requests used User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier. Only extraction/c161.json was written.
